newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Monday:

* Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu avoided charges in an affair over the appointment of an attorney general as Israeli prosecutors said they did not have enough evidence. But they said they had a "tangible suspicion" about the propriety of his involvement in the matter.

* News Analysis: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan seemed in December to indicate the stock market boom was coming to a close. Now, it appears he meant that the speculative frenzy which could foreshadow a market slump has not come yet.
* The union representing 30,000 residential building workers in New York reached a tentative three-year contract, averting a strike.
* In Grand Forks, North Dakota, many worry that miseries caused by flooding could last for weeks.
* Doctors and medical researchers say they have found deep mistrust, among many blacks, of the medical establishment and its AIDS treatments.
* A complex set of steps led to talks this month between tobacco companies, regulators and anti-smoking advocates.
